newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq workers clear hurdle for Duferco buy.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq workers clear hurdle for Duferco buy.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt Belgian steel firm Forges de Clabecq overwhelmingly backed the planned partial takeover by Italian-Swiss group Duferco in a move which looks set to end a six-month fight to preserve jobs.

Of Clabecq's 1,800 workers, 94.5 percent voted for the deal in a referendum organised by the Belgian Labour Ministry, rejecting calls for a boycott by local, maverick union organiser Roberto D'Orazio.
D'Orazio had demanded more jobs guarantees before backing the takeover, but Duferco's had threatened to drop its bid unless it received grassroots support.
The workers' approval leaves three other hurdles to be cleared before the deal can be finalised.
Clabecq's bank creditors need to agree, legal authorities, who have acted as caretakers, must approve it and European Union competition authorities need to give the green light.
Production is to resume in the spring of 1998 with a staff of 893. Former workers of Clabecq, which was declared bankrupt in January, will get preferential treatment when they apply.
Duferco plans to invest 2.8 billion francs in the company over five years.
Duferco agreed a partial purchase with the Walloon region, Clabecq's largest shareholder, earlier this month.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy after the European Commission banned the southern region of Wallonia from injecting 1.5 billion francs ($41 million) into the loss-making firm and ordered the company to reimburse subsidies already granted.
